claims.claim: Eight target TypeInfos (IVar, IVar2, read/write callbacks, IMCCommand and command callback) decode in both resources with 33 methods and zero normalized changes.
CVar2::ReadVarAsync(IVar2) has version-specific entries old VA 0x1000d28a and new VA 0x1000d39c, identical 30-byte entry bytes and Rizin size 690.

The async entry path directly calls version-specific internal transaction code, allocates/initializes a 12-byte transaction/result record, performs capability checks, prepares StartRead-formatted request data, processes result BSTR/VARIANT data and validates a client-handle magic value 0x890abcde.
claims.caveat: shared transaction branches and exact semantics of helper arguments remain unresolved

claims.claim: ReadVarAsync passes caller pReqID to the transaction starter; the starter stores that pointer at transaction offset +0x98, and a downstream completion/result routine writes the generated value through the stored output pointer (old 0x1000ff3e, new 0x10010050).

Completion code directly calls an interface vtable slot +0x14 in old 0x1000fef1/new 0x10010003; nearby code prepares OnDataChanged diagnostics. The exact per-ReadVarAsync linkage and timing remain unresolved.
Both images expose named cyclic creation, request-ID, DataChange, IdleCB, FlushCyclics and removal machinery; TypeLib gives exact method surface.
Cyclic owner likely maintains a linked list with node next at +0x0 and cyclic pointer at node +0x08; repeated accesses show cyclic state/data fields around +0x38,+0x40,+0x74,+0x80.
claims.caveat: constructor-complete layout and field semantics are not proven

claims.claim: DataChange/IdleCB/FlushCyclics and critical-section evidence support an internal stateful update path, but direct causal edges and timer ownership are unresolved.

In the new build, FlushCyclics conditionally calls helper 0x100139c2 at 0x100134ab when state bit 0x80000 at [this+0x28] is set; the helper is a callback-dispatch candidate, but final indirect target and upstream DataChange/IdleCB causality remain unresolved.
ATL interface-map/QI imports, InterlockedDecrement, critical-section calls, and Dispatch/Dual callback diagnostics exist in both binaries.
Callback AddRef/Release, full request/cyclic object lifetime, worker thread, cross-apartment marshaling and exact timer ownership are not established.
Synchronous batch ReadVar remains the only acquisition mode proven by preserved real-PCU logs.
Async/cyclic nonblocking behavior, callback delivery, periodic/change-only semantics, removal, cancellation and reconnect remain runtime unknowns despite static ABI and implementation clues.
